open_points.subject: instance_lifecycle pass scheduling after delayed readings
open_points.text: the n-th call is due when `clock.monotonic_reading` shows n intervals since serving began, the first one interval after; a call due while the previous call of the same pass is still running is not made, and the pass waits for the next due one.
open_points.question: When the monotonic reading jumps across one or more due instants while no previous call is running, does the pass make every overdue call, make one coalesced call immediately, or skip them and wait for the next future due instant?
options: Make every overdue call in order
Make one call immediately and resume the interval grid
Skip overdue calls and wait for the next future due instant
open_points.default_guess: Make one call immediately for each pass and resume at the next interval boundary.

witness.initial: Both passes are idle, and the clock replacement reads 30 seconds after serving began.
events: The host is suspended until the monotonic reading is 210 seconds after serving began.
The lifecycle scheduler resumes and examines the reading.
outcomes: It makes the calls due at 60, 120 and 180 seconds in succession.
It makes one coalesced call, or no call until 240 seconds.
witness.observer: The clock-replacement lifecycle test sees different call counts and times; a due backup can also appear at a different time.

open_points.subject: clock.monotonic_reading callers
open_points.text:
### Callers

`module:owner_sessions`.

### Inputs

None.

### Outputs

One reading in nanoseconds, comparable only with other readings of the same
process.
open_points.question: Is `module:instance_lifecycle` also a caller of `clock.monotonic_reading`, as the Passes convention and `start_instance` require, or must pass timing reach it through some other operation?
options: Add `module:instance_lifecycle` as a direct caller
Keep only `module:owner_sessions` and introduce a separate timer abstraction
Keep only `module:owner_sessions` and let lifecycle use an undeclared host timer
open_points.default_guess: Add `module:instance_lifecycle` as a direct caller and declare its import of `clock.monotonic_reading`.

witness.initial: A test replaces `module:clock` and starts the instance.
events: One pass interval elapses according to the replacement clock.
outcomes: `instance_lifecycle` calls the replaced `clock.monotonic_reading` to decide that the pass is due.
The declared caller list is followed, so lifecycle uses another timing source and the replacement clock receives no lifecycle call.
witness.observer: The lifecycle timing test sees whether the replaced clock controls and records the pass.

open_points.subject: given_values.check_value_forms numeric inputs
open_points.text:
The values as `read_optional_text` and `read_required_text` answered them,
each with the field it fills: an alias; an object kind; a floor area, a
number of rooms, a floor; a customer language; a Customer's kind.
open_points.question: Are floor area, number of rooms and floor supplied to `check_value_forms` as preserved text that this operation parses, or as already typed numeric field values; and which operation rejects a numeric representation that cannot be converted?
options: Pass preserved text and parse it in `check_value_forms`
Decode typed numeric fields before calling `check_value_forms`
Use separate text and numeric variants with an explicit conversion failure
open_points.default_guess: Decode according to the State 6 field types before the call, use the text readers only for textual fields, and report shape or conversion failures at stage (4).

witness.initial: A project create form supplies the number of rooms as the text `2.0`.
outcomes: The value is parsed numerically as two, regarded as a whole number and stored.
The integer field rejects the textual representation `2.0` at stage (4).
witness.observer: The owner sees either an accepted project containing two rooms or an `invalid_request` refusal.

open_points.subject: given_values.check_value_forms failure ordering
open_points.text:
Nothing when every present value is within its form; otherwise every value
outside it, each with its field and its kind: `outside_form` for an alias
over the imported `ALIAS_MAX_CHARACTERS` constant, counted in Unicode code
points, a floor area not greater than the imported
`OBJECT_FLOOR_AREA_MIN_EXCLUSIVE` constant, a number of rooms that is not a
whole number of at least the imported `OBJECT_ROOMS_MIN` constant, a floor
that is not a whole number;
`outside_closed_list` for a kind or language outside its enumeration.
open_points.question: In what deterministic order does the operation return multiple failures of the same kind, so callers can preserve the required refusal ordering?
options: The field order listed in this contract
The order values were supplied by the caller
A model-defined canonical field order
open_points.default_guess: Return failures by the field order listed in this contract, grouped by the caller's Errors-list kind order.

witness.initial: A create supplies an overlong alias, floor area 0 and number of rooms 0.
events: `projects` calls `check_value_forms` with all three present values.
The failures are placed in the stage-(4) refusal.
outcomes: The refusal lists alias, floor area and number of rooms in the contract's field order.
The refusal lists them in request or container iteration order.
witness.observer: The owner and wire-level contract test see a different ordered failure list.

open_points.subject: migration_import mapping cleanliness for Customer kind
open_points.text:
and whether the mapping is clean — no malformed record, no conflict,
no missing value, no given name or alias outside A02's form and at least
one pick — which alone lets the confirmation
step be shown.
open_points.question: Does a given Customer kind outside its enumeration make the mapping non-clean and prevent the confirmation step, as Enforces says, or is cleanliness exactly the stated list, which omits that failure?
options: An invalid Customer kind makes the mapping non-clean
The mapping remains clean but confirmation later refuses it
Add every `check_value_forms` failure explicitly to the cleanliness definition
open_points.default_guess: Every `check_value_forms` failure, including an invalid Customer kind, makes the mapping non-clean and prevents the confirmation step.

witness.initial: A valid kept file has one picked project and one Customer to make; there are no malformed records, conflicts or missing values, and its name and alias are valid.
events: The owner gives that Customer the kind `partnership`, outside the Customer-kind enumeration.
The owner requests the mapping and then its confirmation step.
outcomes: The Outputs definition marks the mapping clean and permits the confirmation step because none of its listed defects exists.
The Enforces passage shows `outside_closed_list`, marks the mapping non-clean and withholds the confirmation step.
witness.observer: The owner sees whether a confirmation form and value are produced.

open_points.subject: file_unreadable for a truncated declared upload
open_points.text: `file_unreadable` — bytes that do not parse as the format States 5 and 6 declare
open_points.question: Must `file_unreadable` also cover a stream that ends before its declared length even when the bytes received form a complete parseable file, or is the kind restricted to bytes that do not parse?
options: Broaden `file_unreadable` to include transport failure and declared-length truncation
Use a separate closed refusal kind for length mismatch
Accept a parseable file despite the premature end
open_points.default_guess: Broaden `file_unreadable` explicitly to include an I/O failure or a body shorter than its declared length.

witness.initial: The request declares a length one byte greater than the body, while the body bytes themselves are a complete valid import file within the size limit.
events: The stream ends before the declared length.
outcomes: The changed operation passage refuses it as `file_unreadable`.
The closed-set definition does not classify it as `file_unreadable` because the received bytes parse successfully, so an implementation accepts it or needs an undeclared kind.
witness.observer: The uploading owner sees either an accepted upload or a `file_unreadable` refusal.

open_points.subject: read_import_mapping body longer than declared length
open_points.text:
a stream that fails or ends before its
declared length is refused as `file_unreadable`, replacing nothing kept and
changing nothing of the session
open_points.question: What happens when the unread stream supplies more bytes than its declared length while remaining within `IMPORT_FILE_MAX_BYTES`: stop at the declared length, read and digest all bytes, or refuse the mismatch?
options: Read exactly the declared length and leave the remainder for connection disposal
Read through the body stream and include every received byte
Refuse a body longer than its declared length as `file_unreadable`
open_points.default_guess: Refuse any declared-length mismatch as `file_unreadable`; the digest and parser must never silently use a prefix or an undeclared suffix.

witness.initial: An upload declares N bytes but its unread body stream yields N+1 bytes, all below the import size limit; only the first N bytes form one valid file.
events: `owner_interface` disposes of anything the operation leaves unread and closes the accepted connection.
outcomes: The operation stops at N, accepts and digests the valid prefix, and the interface discards the last byte.
The operation reads N+1 bytes and either parses a different file or refuses the declared-length mismatch.
witness.observer: The owner sees a different upload result and, if accepted, a different digest and kept file.
